summary.text: A 55-year-old woman with a 20-year history of rheumatoid arthritis had taken hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily for 20 years, with an estimated cumulative dose of 1.46 kg and no previous retinal screening. She was asymptomatic and was referred in 2016 for HCQ retinal toxicity screening.

Parafoveal outer retinal loss and a juxtafoveal hyperautofluorescent area on fundus autofluorescence, consistent with HCQ toxicity, were detected and HCQ was immediately discontinued; BCVA at discontinuation was 0.1 in each eye. Baseline SD-OCT showed parafoveal ellipsoid zone disruption and baseline FAF a symmetrical inferotemporal hyperfluorescent crescent in both eyes. No alternative etiology was identified and genetic testing for inherited retinal dystrophies was negative.

Despite discontinuation, annual follow-up imaging showed continued expansion of the parafoveal atrophic zone and progressive ellipsoid zone loss, FAF at an unstated time showed a hypofluorescent crescent surrounded by hyperfluorescence, and the patient noticed a patch in her vision. Nine years after discontinuation BCVA was stable at 0.12 in each eye while the paracentral scotoma had progressed in both eyes on Humphrey 10-2 fields from 2019 to 2025.
